SECT 01 // OVERVIEW & ARCHITECTURAL FOUNDATIONS

1. Executive Overview & Paradigm Shift

In modern high-fidelity interactive applications (open-world streaming, virtualized micropolygon geometry, multi-gigabyte texture streaming), persistent storage I/O has decisively replaced GPU compute as the primary frame-rate and loading latency bottleneck. While modern Gen4 and Gen5 NVMe solid-state drives sustain raw sequential read throughputs of 7,000 MB/s to 14,000 MB/s, traditional CPU-centric game loading pipelines rarely exceed 1,500 MB/s.

This massive throughput degradation stems from three architectural bottlenecks:

  • OS Kernel Interrupts & Context Switches: Traditional synchronous or standard thread-pool fread / ReadFile invocations trigger excessive roundtrips into the OS scheduler, introducing microsecond-level stalls across tens of thousands of individual asset chunks.
  • CPU Decompression Starvation: Packages compressed with Deflate, Zstandard, or LZ4 saturate host CPU cores during load phases, generating severe frame drops and thread contention against physics and audio systems.
  • Redundant Host-Memory Copies: Data journeys from NVMe into OS page caches, copies into title memory, transitions through driver upload staging buffers, and finally traverses PCIe into VRAM, generating 3x to 4x memory bandwidth amplification.

VolcanStorage is a clean-slate, cross-platform C++20 storage runtime designed specifically for the Vulkan API. It binds asynchronous OS NVMe requests directly to Vulkan staging pipelines, decodes GDeflate-compressed assets on GPU compute units, and synchronizes transfers via 64-bit Timeline Semaphores.

2. Architectural Comparison: VolcanStorage vs Microsoft DirectStorage

DirectStorage addresses storage bottlenecks exclusively within the DirectX 12 ecosystem. VolcanStorage delivers an open, vendor-agnostic architecture designed from inception for cross-platform engines:

Graphics API DirectX 12 Only (Closed D3D12 device binding) Vulkan 1.1 – 1.4 Native (Cross-vendor)

SECT 02 // HARDWARE CAPABILITY PROBE & FACTORY API

3. Deterministic Hardware Downgrade Engine

Consumer devices encompass a vast range of hardware, from integrated APUs to modern flagship GPUs. VolcanStorage implements a deterministic Hardware Capability Probe during factory creation, establishing the optimal hardware path without crashing or failing:

Tier 3: Modern GPU Pipeline (Vulkan 1.3 / 1.4)

12+ GB/s

64-bit Timeline Semaphores (VK_KHR_timeline_semaphore), Vulkan Synchronization2 (VK_KHR_synchronization2), GPU Compute GDeflate, and Resizable BAR Zero-Copy Direct VRAM DMA.

Tier 2: Mainstream Pipeline (Vulkan 1.2 / APUs)

4–8 GB/s

Timeline Semaphores enabled, Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) zero-copy paths on Apple Silicon and AMD/Intel APUs, and multi-threaded CPU SIMD GDeflate fallback when compute queues are saturated.

Tier 1: Universal Compatibility (Vulkan 1.1 Legacy)

1.5–3 GB/s

Standard binary VkFence / VkSemaphore pairs, POSIX pread / Win32 Overlapped I/O, and persistent 64 MB host-visible staging buffer pools.

Zero Crash Guarantee: If target hardware lacks modern extensions, VolcanStorage automatically scales down internal queue dispatchers without triggering Vulkan validation layer warnings or device loss errors.

4. Factory Initialization & Capability Query (C++20)

VolcanStorage provides an ergonomic C++20 interface that decouples storage initialization from your main graphics engine loop:

#include <volcanstorage/volcanstorage.h>

// 4.1. Configure Factory Parameters
volcan::FactoryDesc desc{};
desc.Device = myVulkanDevice;
desc.PhysicalDevice = myPhysicalDevice;
desc.DefaultStagingBufferSize = 64 * 1024 * 1024; // 64 MB staging ring

volcan::IVolcanStorageFactory* factory = nullptr;
VkResult res = volcan::CreateVolcanStorageFactory(&desc, &factory);

if (res == VK_SUCCESS) {
    const volcan::VolcanDeviceCapabilities& caps = factory->GetCapabilities();
    printf("[VolcanStorage] Active Tier: %d | ReBAR: %s | Timelines: %s\n",
        caps.Tier,
        caps.SupportsReBAR ? "ENABLED" : "DISABLED",
        caps.SupportsTimelineSemaphores ? "SUPPORTED" : "EMULATED");
}

SECT 03 // STORAGE QUEUES & ASYNCHRONOUS I/O

5. Asynchronous File Access & Queue Dispatch

VolcanStorage abstracts underlying operating system storage APIs through high-performance, non-blocking asynchronous drivers:

  • Windows: Win32 CreateFileW with FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED | FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING bound to I/O Completion Ports (IOCP).
  • Linux: Native kernel io_uring submission/completion rings paired with sector-aligned O_DIRECT disk descriptors.
  • macOS: Asynchronous POSIX worker pools with zero-copy staging into unified memory.
// Open archive file with direct non-blocking disk access
volcan::IVolcanStorageFile* assetFile = nullptr;
factory->OpenFile(L"Content/Paks/World_Textures.volcan", &assetFile);

// Create dedicated high-priority streaming queue
volcan::QueueDesc qDesc{};
qDesc.Capacity = 2048;                               // 2048 concurrent requests
qDesc.QueuePriority = volcan::Priority::Realtime;   // Immediate camera frustum streaming
qDesc.Name = "FrustumStreamQueue";

volcan::IVolcanStorageQueue* streamQueue = nullptr;
factory->CreateQueue(&qDesc, &streamQueue);

6. Request Descriptor Specification (volcan::Request)

Each load operation is described by an atomic volcan::Request structure dispatched to the storage queue:

Field Identifier C++ Type Specification & Description
File IVolcanStorageFile* Valid file handle obtained via factory->OpenFile().
SourceOffset uint64_t Byte offset within archive (aligned to 4 KB boundary).
SourceSize uint32_t Compressed byte length on persistent disk.
UncompressedSize uint32_t Expected post-decompression byte length.
DestType DestinationType DestinationType::Buffer, Image, or Memory.
Destination.Buffer VkBuffer, Offset Target Vulkan vertex/index/uniform buffer and write offset.
Destination.Image VkImage, Extent, Mip Target texture handle, subresource mip level, and 3D extents.

SECT 04 // GDEFLATE GPU COMPUTE & RESIZABLE BAR

7. GPU Compute Decompression Pipeline (GDeflate)

VolcanStorage standardizes upon NVIDIA GDeflate, an open, royalty-free byte-stream format engineered specifically for massively parallel SIMD/SIMT architectures:

  • Tile-Based Partitioning: Payloads are split into independent 64 KB tiles. Each tile compresses into its own bitstream, allowing thousands of GPU threads to decompress concurrently.
  • Branchless Prefix-Code Decoding: Compute shader workgroups (128 or 256 threads) decode independent tiles simultaneously, eliminating thread divergence penalties.
  • Standard SPIR-V Compute: The decompression kernel is authored in GLSL 450 (shaders/GDeflate.comp) and precompiled to standard SPIR-V bytecodes.
// Core Dispatch Logic (Internal Compute Engine)
void DispatchGDeflateCompute(VkCommandBuffer cmd, uint32_t tileCount) {
    vkCmdBindPipeline(cmd, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_COMPUTE, gDeflatePipeline);
    vkCmdBindDescriptorSets(cmd, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_COMPUTE, 
                            pipelineLayout, 0, 1, &descriptorSet, 0, nullptr);

    // Each Workgroup handles 1 tile (64 KB max payload)
    vkCmdDispatch(cmd, tileCount, 1, 1);
}

Automatic Image Layout Transitions

When DestinationType::Image is targeted, VolcanStorage's internal transfer queue automatically executes barrier transitions inside the compute/transfer command buffers:

VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED → VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL → VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL

Your graphics engine can sample textures immediately upon timeline semaphore completion!

8. Zero-Copy Streaming via Resizable BAR (ReBAR)

Legacy architectures restricted host-to-device PCIe transfer apertures to 256 MB. With Resizable BAR (ReBAR) and AMD Smart Access Memory, the entire VRAM pool is directly addressable in host memory space:

VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT

When detected, NVMe I/O is DMA-transferred directly into device-local memory, eliminating host DRAM staging copies entirely.

SECT 05 // PERSISTENT STAGING & SYNCHRONIZATION

9. Persistent Staging Pool Mechanics

A fatal pitfall in naive Vulkan streaming systems is allocating temporary VkDeviceMemory blocks for each load request. Frequent allocations trigger OS page table faults, memory fragmentation, and severe frame hitching.

  • VolcanStorage pre-allocates a persistent 64 MB host-visible staging ring buffer at startup.
  • Incoming requests acquire sub-allocated offsets into the ring buffer via atomic increments.
  • Completed DMA transfers release ring segments in constant time O(1).
  • Zero runtime heap allocations occur during intense asset streaming operations.

10. Complete Step-by-Step Render Loop Integration (C++20)

This production code example demonstrates an asynchronous load request synchronized with the engine's render loop via 64-bit Timeline Semaphores:

// 1. Create a 64-bit Timeline Semaphore for storage synchronization
VkSemaphoreTypeCreateInfo timelineInfo{
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SEMAPHORE_TYPE_CREATE_INFO,
    .semaphoreType = VK_SEMAPHORE_TYPE_TIMELINE,
    .initialValue = 0
};
VkSemaphoreCreateInfo semInfo{
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SEMAPHORE_CREATE_INFO,
    .pNext = &timelineInfo
};
VkSemaphore storageTimeline;
vkCreateSemaphore(device, &semInfo, nullptr, &storageTimeline);

// 2. Enqueue asynchronous load request
volcan::Request req{};
req.File = worldArchive;
req.SourceOffset = 1048576;     // Byte offset in archive
req.SourceSize = 262144;        // 256 KB compressed on disk
req.UncompressedSize = 1048576; // 1 MB decompressed payload
req.DestType = volcan::DestinationType::Buffer;
req.Destination.Buffer.TargetBuffer = terrainVBO;
req.Destination.Buffer.Offset = 0;

streamQueue->EnqueueRequest(&req);

// 3. Enqueue fence signal at monotonic timeline value 42
uint64_t expectedSyncValue = 42;
streamQueue->EnqueueSignalTimeline(storageTimeline, expectedSyncValue);
streamQueue->Submit();

// 4. Render Loop: Submit graphics command buffer waiting directly on GPU timeline
VkTimelineSemaphoreSubmitInfo timelineWait{
    .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_TIMELINE_SEMAPHORE_SUBMIT_INFO,
    .waitSemaphoreValueCount = 1,
    .pWaitSemaphoreValues = &expectedSyncValue
};
// The draw call executes the exact nanosecond loading and decompression finishes!

SECT 06 // BUILD PIPELINE, PACKAGING & AUDIT

11. Build Pipeline & Automated Packaging

VolcanStorage integrates into standard CMake build systems. It requires a C++20 compliant compiler (MSVC v143+, GCC 12+, Clang 15+) and the Vulkan SDK (version 1.1 or newer):

# In your engine's CMakeLists.txt:
add_subdirectory(third_party/VolcanStorage)
target_link_libraries(MyGameEngine PRIVATE VolcanStorage)

The repository features automated PowerShell packaging tools generating cross-platform distribution archives for 6 distinct target platforms:

# Package all platforms into dist/ directory with SHA-256 digests:
pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/package_release.ps1 -All
